paper_metadata.title: Development of High-Strength High-Temperature Cast Al-Ni-Cr Alloys Through Evolution of a Novel Composite Eutectic Structure

evidence.quote: this article reports a new class of multiphase Al alloys in the Al-Ni-Cr system
This article reports the morphological transition of the eutectic cell during the growth in ternary Al-Ni-Cr alloys with Cr content varying from 0.5 to 0.7 at. pct.
Using binary Al-Al3Ni eutectic (Al-3.1Ni) samples for benchmarking, we have studied three alloys with varying additions of Cr along the line AD (Figure 1).
We shall designate these as Al-4Ni-0.5Cr, Al-4Ni-0.6Cr, and Al-5Ni-0.7Cr.

evidence.quote: After a further deformation of sample to 30 pct, one can observe crack formation with propagation along the weak colony boundaries, as shown in Figure 8(c).
The small solubility of Cr in Al 3Ni rods enhances plasticity of the rods.
The Al3Ni lamellae at the colony boundaries behave in a diﬀerent manner than the rods.
The eutectic colonies are separated by a layer of a-aluminum.
However, the slip band formation is more extensive in this case than in the case of room temperature.
Formation of cracks takes place at the trijunction of the colony boundaries through interaction of shear bands (inset in Figure 8(d)).

mechanisms.name: crack bridging
mechanisms.material_state: as-cast, 30 pct deformed in compression at room temperature

evidence.quote: The presence of hierarchical morphologies of rods and plates in eutectic have helped in increasing the strength and resistance to the fracture. The Al3Ni rods parallel to the crack length either do not interact with the cracks or get pulled off from the matrix (interface debonding).

The plates provide the plasticity either by diverting the crack (as shown in region 5, dotted arrows) or by crack bridging (regions 3 and 4, solid circle in inset and solid rectangle), which are oriented perpendicular to the crack path.
